title: Yet public hymns and litanies ask Mary to pity, free, and give goods—not merely to pray
source_text: LIII. Veruntamen in publico Ecclesiae cultu, orationes multae ad Sanctos diriguntur, in quibus non simpliciter rogantur, ut pro nobis orent, sed ut nostri misereantur, nosque liberent a malis corporis & animae, ac ea bona quibus egemus donent. Sic in hymno qui incipit, Lux Mundi Beatissima, haec ad Beatam Virginem dicuntur: Te adesse deposcimus, Supplicibus nunc vocibus, Jam veni dulcis Domina, Nostra tolle incommoda, Dona confer caelestia. Et in hymno, Ave Maris Stella, ad eandem haec habetur Oratio, Virgo singularis, Inter omnes mitis, Nos culpis solutos, Mites fac & castos. Vitam praesta puram, Iter para tutum, Ut videntes Jesum, Semper collaetemur. In hymno quoque Memento salutis author haec leguntur, Maria Mater gratiae, Mater Misericordiae, Tu nos ab hoste protege, Et hora mortis suscipe. Denique in Antiphona, Alma Redemptoris mater, sic compellatur eadem Maria, Virgo prius ac posterius, Gabrielis ab ore Sumens illud Ave, peccatorum miserere. In Litaniis vero, non usu publico Ecclesiae Rom. receptis, sed Bonaventurae Psalterio adjectis, & in usum plebis Romanae editis, postquam saepius Beatae Virgini sub variis titulis & Elogiis invocatae dictum est, Ora pro Nobis, tandem illi quoque dicitur Propitia esto, Parce nobis Domina, Ab omni malo, libera nos Domina, Ab ira Dei & indignatione ejus, A periculosa desperatione, A superbia praecipitante, A luxuria deturbante, &c. Libera nos Domina. Veni, Peccatores, Te rogamus Audi nos, Ut Sanctam Ecclesiam piissima Domina conservare digneris, Te Rogamus audi nos. Denique dicitur illi Mater cum Filio tuo sanctissimo, Miserere nobis, Mater charissima Domina, Miserere nobis. In Psalterio Dominae nostrae Gallice edito Parisiis apud Claudium Chappelet Anno 1601.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless in the public cult of the Church many prayers are directed to the Saints, in which they are not simply asked to pray for us, but to pity us, and to free us from evils of body and soul, and to give those goods which we need. Thus in the hymn which begins Lux Mundi Beatissima these things are said to the Blessed Virgin: We demand that Thou be present, Now with suppliant voices, Come now sweet Lady, Take away our troubles, Confer heavenly gifts. And in the hymn Ave Maris Stella this prayer is had to the same: Singular Virgin, Mild among all, Make us, loosed from faults, Mild and chaste. Grant a pure life, Prepare a safe way, That seeing Jesus we may always rejoice together. In the hymn also Memento salutis author these things are read: Mary Mother of grace, Mother of Mercy, Protect us from the enemy, And in the hour of death receive us. Finally in the Antiphon Alma Redemptoris mater the same Mary is thus addressed: Virgin before and after, Taking that Ave from Gabriel’s mouth, pity sinners. But in the Litanies, not received by the public use of the Roman Church, but added to Bonaventure’s Psalter and published for the use of the Roman people, after it has often been said to the Blessed Virgin invoked under various titles and Eulogies, Pray for Us, at length it is also said to her Be propitious, Spare us Lady, From every evil free us Lady, From the wrath of God and His indignation, From dangerous despair, From precipitating pride, From overthrowing luxury, etc. Free us Lady. Come, Sinners, We ask Thee Hear us, That Thou most pious Lady wouldst deign to preserve the Holy Church, We ask Thee hear us. Finally it is said to her Mother with Thy most holy Son, Have mercy on us, Most dear Mother Lady, Have mercy on us. In Our Lady’s Psalter published in French at Paris at Claude Chappelet’s in the year 1601.
pass_b_english: Public hymns still ask Mary to pity, free, and confer goods—not only to pray.
Ave Maris Stella, Alma Redemptoris, and Bonaventure-style litanies even say ‘Spare us / Free us, Lady’ and ‘Have mercy.’
